gap: BHD is clean (0 px changed on /customer and /invoice at both viewports, pre-wave vs post-wave, same data; dashboard differs only in an 11x17px 'last refreshed' clock, 11:55 vs 11:57), so the verdict is design, not leakage. Ours wins /customer and loses the screen that decides it. /invoice under pnp: row heights 134.5, 93.9, 93.9, 93.9, 73.6, 73.6, 73.6, 73.6, 73.6, 72.6 px, a 1.86x swing inside one table because client names wrap to five blue underlined lines; the bar's rows are one uniform height with truncation and no underline anywhere. font-variant-numeric is 'normal', so Total and Paid set money in proportional digits (123,456.789 next to 7.500) where the bar's $25,980.23 is a clean numeric column, and each amount is prefixed with a heavy OMR glyph that reads as a smudge. An orange warning triangle plus 'No Payment' repeats on 4 of the first 5 rows, duplicating the Status column, and lands in the same orange as the 'Sent' status, so one colour means both neutral and alarm; the file's own header says the bar carries no chips and no second per-row affordance. ant-table-ping-right is true at 1440, so a grey fixed-column shadow band runs the full height of the table and a whole column is clipped off-screen: 'Payment', whose value is 'Evidence Incomplete' on 10 of 10 rows. On /customer, where the styling is genuinely close to the bar (72px uniform rows, pale non-uppercase header, hairline separators), 3 of 6 columns carry exactly one distinct value across all 10 rows (Type=Company, Location=Oman, Last Activity=dash) and there is no checkbox column although /invoice has one, so the two list pages of the same product disagree. At 390x844 the table drops every column but Name plus a kebab, so the financial data disappears entirely on mobile, under a toolbar of five stacked controls including two unlabelled icon pills sized like primary buttons.
